author: Manu
text:
Ok, I will try too.

I see the symmetry as floors of a building where the price goes from one
 to another. Imagine that the price is a ball. A ball may bounce upward
on the floor or down on the ceiling of a floor. But this ball also has
the ability to cross the floor or ceiling if given circumstances.

The rule is that the ball will only bounce (if it does) on the floor or
ceiling of the floor where it is at the moment (not in the space between
 them wich is the floor itself), and if it crosses for example the
ceiling and goes upstairs, the inertia will take it to the roof of that
new floor (target). Then it could bounce there or cross that roof at
first touch and move to the next floor. That is, if the price comes from
 below, the ceiling of new floor to which it accedes will be the target

Let's see the chart:

The price (ball) reaches the roof of the first floor and does not
bounce, it crosses. We have left the first floor behind and we are
already on the second floor. What happens here? The price begins to
rebound on the roof and the floor several times until finally it crosses
 the ceiling and goes to the third floor. The price has already left the
 second floor and will not be able to cross it back until it reaches the
 roof of the third floor (target).What do we have on the second floor? A
 FLAG. Which are its limits? The floor and ceiling of the second floor.
Floors and ceilings are FLs and can be FTRs, S/R, etc, too. I supose
that at he left the ceilings and floors are respected, too.

What happens on the third floor? Reaches the ceiling and directly
crosses (line 3) to the fourth floor, so it must go to the ceilong of
that new floor (target). What happens on the fourth floor? The ball
(price) bounces a couple of times on ceiling and floor and crosses the
floor returning to the floor below (third floor).

As I said before, the price can only bounce off the floor and ceiling.
As it comes from the ceiling, where could it bounce? On the floor, which
 is in turn the second floor ceiling.

And so on.

So what conclusion can we draw from this symmetry?

The price will always bounce off the ceiling or floor and not anywhere
else inside the floor. Therefore, WE ONLY MUST PLAN THE TRADES AT FLOOR
OR CEILING OF THE FLOOR IN WHICH WE FIND US. OR WHAT IS THE SAME, IN THE
 FLs, FTR, etc.

The engulf of one floor with a Flag inside will shoe us intentions to continue in the direction of the engulf.

In the future, this structure of floors will be respected and the
importance of each floor depend on what you have in the past on that
floor

PD: It is possible that everything I have said is nothing but nonsense.
And i know that my english sometimes sucks, sorry for that.

Aaaaaaand there we have it!

Question and answer in one!!!

Question: If price moves through an array of rectangles, why can't we just draw permanent horizontals and trade from them?

Answer: Because the rectangles shift to align with the kinks, the flag limits which form on the break into the next rectangle!

Remember. There are two different types of IT. The left shoulder trader, and the FL trader. Both are in control

 charts, but i don't see any array. I see that you can draw some lines
and that price changes his behavior after passing through some of them.
But sometimes it doesn't. I also see that if you draw a line on every

Thanks for your answer, i'm completely lost in the desert here...

author: Edge
text:
H, Its all good brother. RTM is best consumed like a piece of meat
marinating and slow cooked breaking down the fibres so it becomes moist
and succulent (for my vegan friends here, apply the analogy to tofu).
Dont rush the experience

In its simplest form the market is flags and poles (this includes
implied flags). Its the interactions of the edges we need to watch. Also
 remember that a CP area is treated as a pole. Within this blueprint of
price we have lines everywhere and the interconnections between flags
and poles which are the kinks.

BUT....... not all these are tradable. We do need to be aware of where
they are for purposes of scale and TGs when in a trade. But We need to
think about which kinks are the best to trade.
